title: Literal Matching
description: Find and match the exact word 'hanami' in the input string (case-sensitive).
hint: Literal characters in regular expressions match themselves exactly. Just type the letters in sequence.

title: Matching Area Codes
description: Extract a 3-digit phone area code enclosed in parentheses. Example: '(123)' should extract '123'.
hint: Parentheses are special metacharacters in regex. To match literal parentheses, escape them with backslashes like \( and \). Use \d with a quantifier like \d{3} to match digits.

title: Word Boundaries
description: Match the exact word 'cat' (case-sensitive). Do not match 'cats', 'category', or 'bobcat'.
hint: Use the word boundary anchor \b at the start and end of the word to assert that it stands alone.

title: Hex Color Codes
description: Validate 3 or 6-digit HTML hex color codes starting with '#'. E.g., '#FFF' or '#FF00AA'.
hint: Use anchors (\A and \z or ^ and $) to match the full string. Use character sets like [a-fA-F0-9] and group alternatives with a pipe | character inside parentheses.

title: Protocol Extraction
description: Extract the protocol ('http' or 'https') from a URL using a named capture group called 'protocol'.
hint: Define a named capture group using the syntax (?<protocol>https?). Remember to match the trailing :// but do not include it inside the group.

title: Positive Lookahead
description: Match any numeric value only if it is immediately followed by the unit 'px' (pixels). E.g. match '120' in '120px' but not in '120em'.
hint: Use a positive lookahead (?=px) after matching the digits (\d+). The lookahead asserts the condition without consuming the 'px' suffix.
